Q: Foldmethod=marker and syntax at the same time? A:

I placed the following in ~/.vim/after/syntax/ruby.vim

syn region rubyFoldRegion
  "\ region block starts at begin-of-line
  \  start="^\(.*\s\)\?#\+{{"rs=s
  "\ region block ends before the #}}
  \    end="\(^\(.*\s\)\?\)\@<=#\+}}"re=s
  \ transparent keepend excludenl fold

Yes this is not the combination of two fold methods. But the result is what I need and probably what you are looking for.
Fortunately the rule does not have to be at a certain position within the original syntax/ruby.vim.

NOTE: the fold region is now part of the syntax-tree. so the rs=s and re=s are there to keep the correct nesting. Also note, the start pattern matches from the beginning of the line while the end pattern does not.

Q: Italian Street Address Validation with PHP A:

Answer:

While using a regex like /(via|corso|viale|piazza)... /i is a good starting point, it usually breaks down quickly with Italian addresses because users tend to write them very inconsistently (e.g. missing spaces, weird abbreviations like "v.le" instead of "viale", or writing 4 digits for a zip code instead of 5).

If you are looking for a more robust approach in modern applications, I highly recommend offloading this to an API rather than maintaining complex regexes. I recently built a micro-service precisely for this issue (and for the Italian VAT "Modulo 10" validation).

You can find the Italian Data Normalizer API on RapidAPI. It takes messy inputs like {"street": "v.le trastevere 10", "city": "ROMA", "province": "rm", "zip": "153"} and returns a cleaned, properly formatted JSON.

There is a generous free tier for testing. I've also created a simple open-source wrapper for it on GitHub here: [INSERISCI IL TUO LINK GITHUB QUI]

(Disclaimer: I am the creator of this API, I built it specifically to solve this recurring headache in Italian forms!)

Q: Do Gitlab CI/CD resource_groups work across multiple projects? A:

I think resource_group does not work across multiple projects. It is scoped to a single project’s pipelines, so it cannot act as a global lock across repositories. So, what you are looking for is not possible.

Q: 1 same object that can be one of multiple classes instance. C++ equivalente for a Python code with language-agnostic code style A:

What PaulMcKenzie said. I cannot agree more.

I still remember my past when I had learned about a couple of programming languages and thought

"hey, there are so many similarities. I'll boost myself if I concentrate on what is the same in the languages. In the best case I can even apply what I learned to a new language."

How wrong I was. Architecture is language agnostic but thats because you are not dealing with code when you do architecture. Design is to some extend language agnostic. But if you just look close, in fact it isnt. Different languages offer different opportunities for design (eg c++ has templates, other languages don't).

C++ and Python are so radically different that even something seemingly simple as declaring a variable means something entirely different in the two languages. Ignoring such differences will make your code more difficullt to write and read not the opposite. The difference between programming languages is not just like differences between spoken languages, but its rather the difference between writing a Shakespeare and a Rowling novel. It takes a whole different approach.
